name: ShieldTech SB-3 'Groundstrike'
description:
The ShieldTech SB-3 is the defining image of private security in GLMZ's middle tiers — a matte-black polycarbonate baton, 58 centimeters long, with a rubberized grip and a pair of exposed copper-alloy contact prongs at the striking end. It delivers a standardized 50,000-volt, low-amperage shock on contact, enough to cause involuntary muscle contraction and temporary incapacitation in most unaugmented adults. The SB-3 charges via a universal inductive pad in roughly four hours and holds enough charge for approximately forty full-power discharges before requiring a cycle.

The SB-3 has been in continuous production since 2161 and has undergone six incremental revisions, each improving ergonomics and discharge reliability without dramatically altering the product's essential character. It is certified under the Meridian Municipal Security Standards MMSS-7 framework, meaning it is legal for licensed security personnel to carry on duty. Off-duty carry requires a standard Tier 2 personal protection permit. The weapon is deliberately simple — no digital components, no wireless connectivity, no firmware to exploit or brick remotely. This is widely regarded as a feature.

ShieldTech markets the SB-3 almost exclusively to building security firms, transit enforcement contractors, and small-business owners in Tier 2 and Tier 3 zones. It is not glamorous. Security trainers across the city use it as a teaching tool precisely because it is predictable and honest about what it is.
legality: Licensed — legal with standard Tier 2 personal protection permit or active security contractor credentials
specifications: Length: 580mm Weight: 620g Discharge Voltage: 50,000V Amperage: 0.003A (fixed) Charge Capacity: ~40 full discharges Charge Time: 4 hours (inductive) Contact Type: Dual copper-alloy prong Grip: Rubberized over-mold, ambidextrous Body: Matte polycarbonate composite Price: Φ180
tactical_use: The SB-3 is used at close range as a contact weapon — pressed or struck against an attacker to deliver a shock that disrupts voluntary muscle control for three to eight seconds in most subjects. Security personnel are trained to follow a shock with a verbal command and physical control technique before the subject recovers. The weapon's lack of a ranged delivery mechanism means it requires the user to close distance, which is its primary tactical limitation. In crowd management situations, the visible presence of the SB-3 is often sufficient deterrent without discharge.
cultural_context: On the street, the SB-3 is called 'the three' or just 'the stick.' It is so ubiquitous in Tier 2 and Tier 3 security contexts that it has become almost invisible — the visual shorthand for underpaid, slightly bored building security. Getting 'three'd' means being shocked by one, and carries a faint social embarrassment in addition to the physical unpleasantness. In Tier 1 slang, any baton regardless of make is sometimes called a 'groundstrike' after the SB-3's product designation.
story_hooks: A wave of SB-3 units in a specific production batch have been found to deliver irregular, potentially lethal amperage spikes — ShieldTech is quietly recalling them, but thousands are still in service and the company wants the information suppressed until after a major contract renewal.
related_entities: CortexDynamics VectorLink Pro Pilot Neural Interface

physical_description.visual_profile: A no-nonsense security baton with utilitarian aggression — cylindrical shaft tapering to a striking head crowned by two prominent copper prongs. The silhouette reads as honest industrial tool rather than lethal hardware. At rest, it suggests competent force without theater.
physical_description.dimensions: 58 cm (580 mm) length overall. Striking head widens to approximately 4 cm diameter where prongs mount. Prongs extend 1.2 cm beyond the head surface.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and purposeful in hand — 620 grams distributed to center of mass slightly forward of grip. Hefty enough to feel authoritative without fatigue on extended carry. Swings with deliberate momentum.
physical_description.primary_material: Polycarbonate composite body — impact-resistant polymer engineered for duty cycle abuse. Copper-alloy contact prongs provide electrical conductivity and limited corrosion resistance.
physical_description.finish: Matte black polycarbonate, deliberately non-reflective. No shine, no gloss — absorbs light to avoid drawing attention. Surface shows micro-texturing for grip security even when wet. Prongs display natural copper-gold oxidation with faint green patina in service-worn units.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal-black body dominating. Dual copper-alloy prongs in warm metallic gold-bronze at the head, providing the only chromatic accent. Rubberized grip band in textured black.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized over-mold with cross-hatch diamond pattern, ambidextrous — no handed preference. Slightly tacky polymer compound maintains purchase through sweat or moisture. Raised ridges at intervals for finger positioning during power strikes.
distinctive_features: Dual asymmetrical copper-alloy contact prongs angled outward at 15 degrees for maximum surface contact
Shallow circumferential grooves along shaft for structural reinforcement and visual segmentation
Inductive charging port recessed 3 cm from pommel (small circular pad, barely visible)
Faint embossed SHIELDTECH logo on upper grip section
Subtle witness marks where prongs meet head — stress relief geometry visible on close inspection
Pommel capped with slightly domed end in matching matte black
Micro-abrasion marks typical of duty carry on belt hardware
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ShieldTech wordmark embossed (not printed) at 12 o'clock on grip section, roughly 8 cm from pommel. Serial number stamped on underside of pommel. Model designation 'SB-3' and revision number acid-etched into polymer near striking head. Meridian Municipal Standards certification stamp (MMSS-7) on grip, wear-resistant.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained specimens show uniform matte finish with no chips or cracks. High-use units (1-2 years duty) accumulate micro-scratches on prongs from contact training, slight shine on grip from hand oils, and fading of inductive pad cover. Field-worn examples may show impact divots on shaft and blackened carbon residue on prongs from repeated discharge.
